title: DFA Exercise: Contains 'aa' vs Ends in 'aa'
description: A run_dfa function and two machine dicts: CONTAINS_AA with TODO transitions to fill in, and ENDS_IN_AA already complete. Seven test strings show the difference between containing a substring and ending with it. The TODO hints: once 'aa' is seen, no later input can un-see it.

steps.description: run_dfa generic runner: gets start state, loops over chars, checks delta, updates state, returns True if final state in accept set.

CONTAINS_AA machine: start='q0', accept={'q_seen'}. delta has q0 filled (a->q_a, b->q0), q_a and q_seen have TODO placeholders. Hint: q_seen loops to itself on both inputs because once seen, always seen.
q_a on 'a' should go to q_seen (found 'aa'), on 'b' should go to q0 (run broken). q_seen on both should stay q_seen (absorbing accept).

steps.question: What should q_a transition to on 'b', and why?
steps.answer: q0, because a 'b' breaks the consecutive 'a' run and we must start over looking for 'aa'

steps.description: ENDS_IN_AA machine (complete): start='p0', accept={'p_aa'}. p0 a->p_a, b->p0. p_a a->p_aa, b->p0. p_aa a->p_aa, b->p0. Note p_aa on 'b' goes to p0 because the string no longer ends in 'aa'.
Key difference: ENDS_IN_AA p_aa on 'b' -> p0 (must end in aa), but CONTAINS_AA q_seen on 'b' -> q_seen (once seen, always accepted).
Test loop compares both machines on 7 strings: 'aa', 'aab', 'baa', 'baab', 'aba', 'b', ''.
Current output (with TODOs unfilled): all CONTAINS_AA results are False because '?' not in delta. ENDS_IN_AA shows 'aa'->True, 'baa'->True, others False.
Expected once filled: machines agree on 'aa' and 'baa', disagree on 'aab' and 'baab' (contain 'aa' but don't end in it).
